ResearchDossier.summary: The brain's forward model predicts the sensory consequences of self-produced movement and attenuates them, so self-tickling feels weak. In a 1999 UCL robot study (16 people), tickliness rose with delay between movement and touch; at 200–300 ms it no longer differed significantly from external touch. Self-produced touch activates somatosensory cortex and anterior cingulate less; the cerebellum may generate the prediction. The mechanism appears abnormal in some patients with auditory hallucinations or passivity experiences.
ResearchDossier.angle: Your brain cancels the touch it sees coming.

Script.headline: Why You Can't Tickle Yourself
Script.cta: Try to tickle yourself right now.

lines.text: Try to tickle yourself. It doesn't work. And your brain is the reason.
Every time you move, your brain predicts exactly what you're about to feel.
When the touch matches that prediction, your brain turns the feeling down.
So your own fingers can never surprise you.
Your own touch even feels less intense, and less pleasant.
In 1999, scientists in London built a tickle robot.
People moved one hand, and the robot stroked the other.
With no delay, it barely tickled.
But add a fifth of a second of delay, and it tickled like someone else's touch.
Most of them never even noticed the delay. Their brains did.
Brain scans agree. Touch areas react less when the touch is your own.
And the cerebellum, at the back of your brain, seems to make the prediction.
In some people who hear voices, that prediction misfires, and their own touch feels like someone else's.
So tickling only works when your brain can't see it coming.
Try it right now. Then tell me: can you tickle yourself?

PublishCopy.title: Why you can't tickle yourself
PublishCopy.description:
Try to tickle yourself. It doesn't work, and your brain is the reason.
Your brain predicts what every movement will feel like and turns the feeling down. In a 1999 experiment at University College London, a tickle robot barely tickled when people controlled it themselves. Add a fifth of a second of delay, and it tickled like someone else's touch.

Try it now. Can you tickle yourself?
